\chapter{Boolean Analysis — General Hypercontractivity}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Cube.General
\section{Overview}

This module lifts one-bit hypercontractivity to the $n$-dimensional cube. It introduces
the $\rho$-correlated noise kernel $K_\rho$, rewrites the noise operator $T_\rho$ and the
inner product $\inn{f, T_\rho g}$ as kernel-weighted sums, and proves an induction theorem
saying that a two-function hypercontractive bound on one bit propagates to all $n$. Building
on the associated two-point inequalities, it derives the low-norms, bridging, and high-norms
one-function hypercontractivity theorems, and finally the general one-function and
two-function hypercontractivity theorems.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\subsection{The noise kernel}

\begin{definition}[Noise kernel of $\rho$-correlated pairs]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p008-b007,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p009-b001,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p009-b002
}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
Let $n$ be a natural number. For $\rho \in \bbr$ and $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$, define
\[
  K_\rho(x,y)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\frac{1+\rho\,\sigma(x_i)\,\sigma(y_i)}{2},
\]
where $\sigma(0)=1$ and $\sigma(1)=-1$. For $|\rho|\le1$, this is the conditional
transition probability from $x$ to $y$ under $\rho$-correlated noise; the joint
probability of a correlated pair with uniform first point is $2^{-n}K_\rho(x,y)$.
The product defines a real-valued kernel for every real $\rho$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of the noise kernel]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_nonneg}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\rho$ be real with $0\le\rho\le1$.
For every $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$,
\[
  K_\rho(x,y)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\frac{1+\rho\,\sigma(x_i)\,\sigma(y_i)}{2}\ge0,
\]
where $\sigma(0)=1$ and $\sigma(1)=-1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier form of the noise kernel]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_fourier_kernel}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_fourier_kernel}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, every real number $\rho$ and all points $x, y$ of the Boolean hypercube $\{0,1\}^n$,
\[
  \sum_{S \subseteq [n]} \rho^{\abs{S}}\,\chi_S(x)\,\chi_S(y)
  \;=\; \prod_{i=1}^{n} \bigl(1 + \rho\,\sigma(x_i)\,\sigma(y_i)\bigr),
\]
where the sum ranges over all subsets $S$ of $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, $\chi_S$ is the
Walsh--Fourier character indexed by $S$, and $\sigma$ is the sign encoding sending
$0\mapsto 1$ and $1\mapsto -1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noise operator as a kernel sum]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_eq_kernel_sum}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_eq_kernel_sum}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_fourier_kernel, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{3}
Fix $\rho \in \bbr$, an arity $n$, and a point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$. For every Boolean
function $g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, the value of the noise operator $T_\rho$ at $x$
equals the kernel-weighted sum of $g$, namely
\[
  (T_\rho g)(x) \;=\; \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^n} K_\rho(x,y)\, g(y),
\]
where $K_\rho(x,y) = \prod_{i} \tfrac{1 + \rho\,\sigma(x_i)\,\sigma(y_i)}{2}$ is the
noise kernel and $\sigma$ is the $\pm 1$ sign encoding of a bit.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noise inner product as a double sum]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.innerProduct_noiseOp_eq_weighted_sum}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.innerProduct_noiseOp_eq_weighted_sum}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_eq_kernel_sum, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a dimension $n$ and a real number $\rho$. For any two Boolean functions $f, g :
\{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, the $L^2$ inner product of $f$ with the noised function $T_\rho g$
can be written as a kernel-weighted double sum:
\[
\langle f, T_\rho g\rangle \;=\; 2^{-n} \sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^n} \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^n}
K_\rho(x,y)\, f(x)\, g(y),
\]
where $K_\rho(x,y) = \prod_{i} \tfrac{1 + \rho\,\sigma(x_i)\,\sigma(y_i)}{2}$ is the
noise kernel and $\sigma$ is the $\pm 1$ sign encoding of a bit.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of kernel-weighted expectations]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.corrExpect_mono}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.corrExpect_mono}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a dimension $n$ and a correlation parameter $\rho$ with $0 \le \rho \le 1$, and let
$K_\rho(x,y) = \prod_{i} \tfrac{1 + \rho\,\chi(x_i)\,\chi(y_i)}{2}$ denote the noise
kernel on the Boolean hypercube $\{0,1\}^n$, where $\chi(0)=1$ and $\chi(1)=-1$. If $h, h' : \{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ satisfy $h(x,y) \le h'(x,y)$
for all $x$ and $y$, then the kernel-weighted average of $h$ is at most that of $h'$:
\[
  \frac{1}{2^n}\sum_{x}\sum_{y} K_\rho(x,y)\, h(x,y)
  \;\le\;
  \frac{1}{2^n}\sum_{x}\sum_{y} K_\rho(x,y)\, h'(x,y).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noise kernel factorization along the final coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_snoc}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_snoc}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a natural number $n$, $\rho \in \bbr$, and points $x', y'$ in the Boolean hypercube $\{0,1\}^n$, and bits $b,
b'$. Write $(x', b)$ and $(y', b')$ for the points of $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ obtained by
appending $b$ and $b'$, respectively, as the final coordinate. Then the noise kernel of
the extended pair factors as
\[
  K_\rho\bigl((x', b),\, (y', b')\bigr)
  \;=\; K_\rho(x', y') \cdot \frac{1 + \rho\,\chi(b)\,\chi(b')}{2},
\]
where $\chi(0)=1$ and $\chi(1)=-1$.
\end{lemma}

\subsection{Fubini-style decompositions}

\begin{lemma}[Iterated expectation on the cube]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_succ_eq_iterated}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_succ_eq_iterated}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_boolCube_succ, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.uniformWeight_succ, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $h : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function on $n+1$ bits. Writing $(x', b)
\in \{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}$ for the point of $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ obtained by appending the
bit $b$ to $x'$ as its last coordinate, the uniform expectation of $h$ can be computed
by first averaging over the last bit and then over the remaining $n$ bits:
\[
  \E[h] \;=\; \E_{x' \in \{0,1\}^n}\Bigl[\tfrac12\bigl(h(x', 0) + h(x', 1)\bigr)\Bigr].
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Final-coordinate moment decomposition]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.norm_collapse_rpow}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.norm_collapse_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_succ_eq_iterated, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p > 0$ and let $f : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function of arity $n+1$.
Writing $(x', b) \in \{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}$ for the point of $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ whose
first $n$ coordinates are $x'$ and whose last coordinate is $b$, one has
\[
  \E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^p\,\bigr]
  \;=\;
\E_{x' \in \{0,1\}^n}\!\left[\tfrac12\Bigl(\abs{f(x', 0)}^p + \abs{f(x',
1)}^p\Bigr)\right],
\]
where both expectations are taken with respect to the uniform measure on the respective
hypercubes.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Last-coordinate decomposition of the noise-kernel average]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.weighted_sum_succ_decomp}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.weighted_sum_succ_decomp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_snoc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_boolCube_succ, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.uniformWeight_succ, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{5}
Fix a natural number $n$, a real number $\rho$, and a function $F \colon \{0,1\}^{n+1} \times \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to
\bbr$ on pairs of points of the Boolean hypercube of dimension $n+1$. Write $\chi(0)=1$ and $\chi(1)=-1$ for
the sign encoding of a bit, $K_\rho(x,y)=\prod_i\frac{1+\rho\chi(x_i)\chi(y_i)}{2}$ for the noise kernel, and
$(x',b)$ for the point of $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ obtained by appending the bit $b$
to $x' \in \{0,1\}^n$. Then
\[
  \frac{1}{2^{\,n+1}}\sum_{x}\sum_{y} K_\rho(x,y)\, F(x,y)
  =
  \frac{1}{2^{\,n}}\sum_{x'}\sum_{y'} K_\rho(x',y')\,
  \Biggl[\frac12 \sum_{b}\sum_{b'} \frac{1+\rho\,\chi(b)\,\chi(b')}{2}\,
  F\bigl((x',b),(y',b')\bigr)\Biggr],
\]
where $x,y$ range over $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$, the points $x',y'$ range over $\{0,1\}^{n}$, and
the bits $b,b'$ range over $\{0,1\}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Slice sum as a one-bit inner product]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_slice_eq_innerProduct}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_slice_eq_innerProduct}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{4}
Fix a natural number $n$, a real number $\rho$, Boolean functions $f, g : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$, and points
$x', y' \in \{0,1\}^n$. For a bit $b$, write $(x', b)$ for the point of $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$
obtained by appending $b$ as the last coordinate of $x'$, and let $\sigma$ denote the
sign encoding with $\sigma(0)=1$ and $\sigma(1)=-1$. Then
\[
  \frac12 \sum_{b \in \{0,1\}} \sum_{b' \in \{0,1\}}
    \frac{1 + \rho\,\sigma(b)\,\sigma(b')}{2}\,
    f(x', b)\, g(y', b')
  \;=\;
  \langle F,\; T_\rho G\rangle,
\]
where $F, G : \{0,1\}^1 \to \bbr$ are the one-bit slices $F(t) = f(x', t_0)$ and $G(t) =
g(y', t_0)$, and the inner product and the noise operator $T_\rho$ are taken on the
one-dimensional cube $\{0,1\}^1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Norm of a one-bit slice]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_norm_slice}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_norm_slice}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a natural number $n$ and $p > 0$, let $f : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function, and let $x' \in
\{0,1\}^n$. Writing $(x', b) \in \{0,1\}^{n+1}$ for the point obtained by appending a
bit $b \in \{0,1\}$ to $x'$, and taking the expectation over the single free bit under
the uniform measure, one has
\[
  \Bigl(\E_{b \in \{0,1\}}\bigl[\,\abs{f(x', b)}^p\,\bigr]\Bigr)^{1/p}
  \;=\;
  \left(\frac{\abs{f(x', 0)}^p + \abs{f(x', 1)}^p}{2}\right)^{1/p}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Final-coordinate averaging preserves the power mean]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.norm_collapse_clean}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.norm_collapse_clean}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.norm_collapse_rpow, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p \ge 1$ and let $f : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function on the
$(n+1)$-dimensional cube. For a point $x' \in \{0,1\}^n$, write $(x',0)$ and $(x',1)$
for the two extensions of $x'$ obtained by appending a final bit. Then averaging over
the last coordinate leaves the expected $p$-th power of $\abs{f}$ unchanged:
\[
  \E_{x' \in \{0,1\}^n}\!\left[\frac{\abs{f(x',0)}^p + \abs{f(x',1)}^p}{2}\right]
  \;=\; \E_{x \in \{0,1\}^{n+1}}\!\bigl[\abs{f(x)}^p\bigr],
\]
where both expectations are taken with respect to the uniform measure.
\end{lemma}

\subsection{H\"older and contraction bounds}

\begin{lemma}[Hölder's inequality for Boolean functions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_ineq_bool}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_ineq_bool}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p > 1$ and let $f, h : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be Boolean functions, with expectations
taken under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$. Then their $L^2$ inner product satisfies
\[
  \langle f, h\rangle \;\le\; \bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{f}^{p}\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p}\,
  \bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{h}^{p/(p-1)}\bigr]\bigr)^{(p-1)/p},
\]
where the exponents $p$ and $p/(p-1)$ are conjugate.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[$L^q$ contractivity of the one-bit noise operator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_Lp_contraction_one_bit}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_Lp_contraction_one_bit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_val_false, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_val_true, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{6}
Let $q \ge 1$ and let $\rho$ be a real number with $0 \le \rho \le 1$. Then for every
Boolean function $g \colon \{0,1\}^1 \to \bbr$ on a single bit, the noise operator
$T_\rho$ satisfies
\[
  \bigl(\E\!\left[\,\abs{T_\rho g}^{\,q}\,\right]\bigr)^{1/q}
  \;\le\;
  \bigl(\E\!\left[\,\abs{g}^{\,q}\,\right]\bigr)^{1/q},
\]
where both expectations are taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^1$.
\end{lemma}

\subsection{Induction from one bit to $n$ bits}

\begin{lemma}[Two-function hypercontractivity in dimension zero]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_func_hyp_zero}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_func_hyp_zero}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p, q \ge 1$ and let $\rho \in \bbr$ be arbitrary. For any two Boolean functions $f,
g : \{0,1\}^0 \to \bbr$ on the zero-dimensional cube, the $L^2$ inner product of $f$
with the noise-operator image $T_\rho g$ satisfies
\[
\langle f, T_\rho g\rangle \;\le\;
\bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{f}^p\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p}\,\bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{g}^q\bigr]\bigr)^{1/q},
\]
where $\E$ denotes expectation under the uniform measure.
\end{lemma}

\langle f, T_\rho g\rangle \;\le\;

\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
Fix exponents $p, q \ge 1$ and a noise parameter $\rho$ with $0 \le \rho \le 1$, and
write $T_\rho$ for the associated noise operator. Suppose the two-function bound
\[
\langle f, T_\rho g\rangle \;\le\;
\bigl(\E[\abs{f}^p]\bigr)^{1/p}\,\bigl(\E[\abs{g}^q]\bigr)^{1/q}
\]
holds for every pair of Boolean functions $f, g \colon \{0,1\}^1 \to \bbr$ on the
one-dimensional cube. Then, for every $n$, the same inequality holds for every pair of
Boolean functions $f, g \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $1 \le p \le 2$ and $1 \le q \le 2$, and set $\rho = \sqrt{(p-1)(q-1)}$. Then for
any two Boolean functions $f, g : \{0,1\}^1 \to \bbr$ on a single bit,
\[
\inn{f, T_\rho g} \;\le\;
\bigl(\E[\,\abs{f}^p\,]\bigr)^{1/p}\,\bigl(\E[\,\abs{g}^q\,]\bigr)^{1/q},
\]
where $T_\rho$ is the noise operator, $\E[\cdot]$ is the expectation, and
$\inn{\cdot,\cdot}$ is the $L^2$ inner product, all taken with respect to the uniform
measure on $\{0,1\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Equivalence of one- and two-function hypercontractivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_function_iff_two_function_hypercontractivity}
\proofsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p003-b007,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b001
}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_function_iff_two_function_hypercontractivity}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p003-b007,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b001
}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p013-b002,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p013-b003
}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_rpow_abs_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_ineq_bool, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_sharpness, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{5}
Fix a natural number $n$. Let $1 \le p \le q$ with $q \ge 2$, and let $\rho$ satisfy $0 \le \rho \le 1$ together
with $\rho \le \sqrt{(p-1)/(q-1)}$. Then the one-function hypercontractive inequality
\[
\bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{T_\rho f}^q\bigr]\bigr)^{1/q} \le
\bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{f}^p\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p}
  \qquad \text{for every Boolean function } f
\]
holds if and only if the dual two-function inequality
\[
\langle f, T_\rho g\rangle \le
\bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{f}^{q/(q-1)}\bigr]\bigr)^{(q-1)/q}\,\bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{g}^p\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p}
  \qquad \text{for every pair of Boolean functions } f, g
\]
holds, where $T_\rho$ is the noise operator and $\E$ and
$\langle\,\cdot\,,\cdot\,\rangle$ are the expectation and $L^2$ inner product with
respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_induction, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.weak_two_function_hypercontractivity_one_bit, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p, q \in \bbr$ satisfy $1 \le p \le 2$ and $1 \le q \le 2$, and set $\rho =
\sqrt{(p-1)(q-1)}$. Then for every $n \in \bbn$ and all Boolean functions $f, g :
\{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$,
\[
\langle f,\, T_\rho g\rangle \;\le\;
\bigl(\E[\,\abs{f}^p\,]\bigr)^{1/p}\,\bigl(\E[\,\abs{g}^q\,]\bigr)^{1/q},
\]
where $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the $L^2$ inner product under the uniform measure
on $\{0,1\}^n$, $\E$ is the corresponding expectation, and $T_\rho$ is the noise
operator with parameter $\rho$.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Stochasticity of the kernel and trivial contractivity}

\begin{lemma}[Noise kernel rows sum to one]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_right}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_right}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0\le\rho\le1$, and fix $x\in\{0,1\}^n$.
The noise kernel
$K_\rho(x,y)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\frac{1+\rho\,\sigma(x_i)\,\sigma(y_i)}{2}$,
where $\sigma(0)=1$ and $\sigma(1)=-1$, satisfies
\[
  \sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^n}K_\rho(x,y)=1.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noise kernel sums to one over the cube]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_left}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_left}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_right}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0\le\rho\le1$, and fix $y\in\{0,1\}^n$.
The noise kernel
$K_\rho(x,y)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\frac{1+\rho\,\sigma(x_i)\,\sigma(y_i)}{2}$,
where $\sigma(0)=1$ and $\sigma(1)=-1$, satisfies
\[
  \sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}K_\rho(x,y)=1.
\]
Thus $K_\rho(\cdot,y)$ is a probability distribution on the cube.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Jensen bound for powers of the noise operator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_abs_rpow_le_kernel_avg}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_abs_rpow_le_kernel_avg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_right, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_eq_kernel_sum, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $T_\rho$ denote the noise operator with parameter
$\rho \in [0,1]$ acting on Boolean functions $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$. Then for every
real exponent $s \ge 1$ and every point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$,
\[
  \abs{(T_\rho f)(x)}^{s} \;\le\; \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^n} K_\rho(x,y)\,\abs{f(y)}^{s},
\]
where $K_\rho(x,y) = \prod_{i} \tfrac{1 + \rho\,\sigma(x_i)\,\sigma(y_i)}{2}$ is the
noise kernel, with $\sigma(0)=1$ and $\sigma(1)=-1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Contractivity of the noise operator in $L^s$]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.trivial_contractivity}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.trivial_contractivity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_left, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_abs_rpow_le_kernel_avg, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $s \ge 1$ and $\rho \in [0,1]$, and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean
function. Then, with expectations taken under the uniform measure on the cube, the noise
operator $T_\rho$ satisfies
\[
  \bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{T_\rho f}^{s}\bigr]\bigr)^{1/s}
  \;\le\;
  \bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{f}^{s}\bigr]\bigr)^{1/s}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_rpow_abs_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_ineq_bool, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_sharpness, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_self_adjoint}
\difficulty{6}
Fix a natural number $n$, exponents $p,q>1$ and a noise parameter $\rho$ with $0 \le \rho \le 1$, and write
$p' = p/(p-1)$ and $q' = q/(q-1)$ for the H\"older conjugates. Then the noise operator
$T_\rho$ on Boolean functions $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ satisfies the $(p \to q)$ bound
\[
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{T_\rho f}^q\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/q} \;\le\;
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^p\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p}
  \qquad \text{for every } f
\]
if and only if it satisfies the conjugate $(q' \to p')$ bound
\[
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{T_\rho f}^{p'}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p'} \;\le\;
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^{q'}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/q'}
  \qquad \text{for every } f,
\]
where all norms are taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{lemma}

\subsection{The bridging case}

\begin{lemma}[Square root of a ratio bounded by one]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Interpolation.sqrt_div_le_one}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Interpolation.sqrt_div_le_one}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers with $0 \le a$, $0 < b$, and $a \le b$. Then $\sqrt{a/b}
\le 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noise-parameter identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_param_eq}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_param_eq}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $p, u \in \bbr$ with $u > 1$. Then
\[
  \Bigl(\frac{u}{u-1} - 1\Bigr)(p-1) \;=\; \frac{p-1}{u-1}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Interpolation.sqrt_div_le_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_param_eq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_function_iff_two_function_hypercontractivity, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.weak_two_function_hypercontractivity, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{5}
Fix a natural number $n$. Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function, and let $p,u\in\bbr$ satisfy $1\le p\le
2\le u$. Set $\rho=\sqrt{(p-1)/(u-1)}$ and let $T_\rho$ denote the noise operator with
parameter $\rho$. Then
\[
  \bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{T_\rho f}^{\,u}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/u}
  \;\le\;
  \bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^{\,p}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p},
\]
where the expectations are taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Real analytic ingredients for the low-norms case}

\begin{lemma}[Interpolation parameters for the low-norms case]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.low_norms_interpolation_params}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.low_norms_interpolation_params}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $p, u, \rho$ be real numbers with $1 < p < u < 2$, and suppose $\rho^2 =
(p-1)/(u-1)$. Then there exist real numbers $\theta \in (0,1)$ and $s > 0$ such that
\[
  \frac{1}{p} = \frac{\theta}{1+\rho^2} + \frac{1-\theta}{s}
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \frac{1}{u} = \frac{\theta}{2} + \frac{1-\theta}{s}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Symmetric power average is at least one]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avg_rpow_ge_one}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avg_rpow_ge_one}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $p \ge 1$ be a real number and let $b \in [0,1]$. Then
\[
  1 \;\le\; \frac{(1+b)^p + (1-b)^p}{2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of symmetric convex sums]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.convex_sym_sum_mono}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.convex_sym_sum_mono}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $f\colon\bbr\to\bbr$ be convex on the half-line $[0,\infty)$, and let $x,y$ be real
numbers with $0 \le x \le y \le 1$. Then
\[
  f(1+x) + f(1-x) \;\le\; f(1+y) + f(1-y).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Antitonicity in the exponent for nonpositive powers]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rpow_sum_antitone_exponent}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rpow_sum_antitone_exponent}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $0 < x < 1$, and let $p \le q \le 0$ be real exponents. Then
\[
  (1+x)^p + (1-x)^p \;\ge\; (1+x)^q + (1-x)^q.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A two-point convexity inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.h_alpha_ineq}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.h_alpha_ineq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rpow_sum_antitone_exponent}
\difficulty{7}
Let $r,s\in\bbr$ satisfy $0\le r\le s\le1$, let $t\in[0,1]$, and set
$c=\sqrt{r/s}$ when $s>0$ and $c=0$ when $s=0$. With $0^0=1$, one has
\[
  (1+t)^r-(1-t)^r\ge c\bigl((1+ct)^s-(1-ct)^s\bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrated two-point hypercontractive inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.integrated_h_alpha_ineq}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.integrated_h_alpha_ineq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.h_alpha_ineq}
\difficulty{6}
Let $p,q,b\in\bbr$ satisfy $1\le p\le q\le2$ and $0\le b\le1$.
Set $\rho=\sqrt{(p-1)/(q-1)}$ when $q>1$ and $\rho=0$ when $q=1$. Then
\[
  \frac{(1+\rho b)^q+(1-\rho b)^q-2}{q}
  \le\frac{(1+b)^p+(1-b)^p-2}{p}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Tangent line inequality for $x^r$ at $x=1$]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rpow_ge_one_add_mul_sub}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rpow_ge_one_add_mul_sub}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every real number $x \ge 0$ and every exponent $r \ge 1$, the power $x^r$ lies above
its tangent line at $x = 1$; that is,
\[
x^r \ge 1 + r\,(x - 1).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[General two-point inequality, unit case]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_point_ineq_general_unit}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_point_ineq_general_unit}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p001-b002}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b002
}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.integrated_h_alpha_ineq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rpow_ge_one_add_mul_sub}
\difficulty{5}
Let $p,q,b\in\bbr$ satisfy $1\le p\le q\le2$ and $0\le b\le1$.
Set $\rho=\sqrt{(p-1)/(q-1)}$ when $q>1$ and $\rho=0$ when $q=1$. Then
\[
  \frac{(1+\rho b)^q+(1-\rho b)^q}{2}
  \le\left(\frac{(1+b)^p+(1-b)^p}{2}\right)^{q/p}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Low, high, and general hypercontractivity}

\begin{theorem}[One-bit low-norms hypercontractivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.low_norms_one_bit}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.low_norms_one_bit}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b006,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b002
}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p001-b002}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_abs_rpow_one_bit, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_point_ineq_general_unit, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{7}
Let $1 < p \le q \le 2$, let $f : \{0,1\}^1 \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function of arity
$1$, and set $\rho = \sqrt{(p-1)/(q-1)}$. Then, with expectations taken under the
uniform measure and $T_\rho$ the noise operator,
\[
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{T_\rho f}^q\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/q} \;\le\;
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^p\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Low-norms cube hypercontractivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.low_norms_hypercontractivity}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.low_norms_hypercontractivity}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p002-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b003,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b002
}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p001-b002}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Interpolation.sqrt_div_le_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.bridging_hypercontractivity, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_rpow_abs_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_ineq_bool, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_sharpness, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_induction, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.low_norms_one_bit, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.trivial_contractivity, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{6}
Fix a dimension $n$ and real exponents $p, u$ with $1 < p \le u \le 2$, and set the
noise rate
\[
  \rho \;=\; \sqrt{\frac{p-1}{u-1}} \;\in\; (0,1].
\]
Then for every function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ on the Boolean hypercube, the noise
operator $T_\rho$ contracts $L^p$ into $L^u$:
\[
  \bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{T_\rho f}^{\,u}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/u}
  \;\le\;
  \bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^{\,p}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p},
\]
where the expectations are taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[High-norms hypercontractivity for the noise operator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.high_norms_hypercontractivity}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.high_norms_hypercontractivity}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p002-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007
}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p001-b002}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Interpolation.sqrt_div_le_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.low_norms_hypercontractivity, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_compose, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_op_norm_dual, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.trivial_contractivity, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{5}
Fix a natural number $n$. Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function, and let $p, u$ be real exponents
with $2 \le p \le u$. Suppose $\rho \in \bbr$ satisfies $0 \le \rho \le 1$ together with
$\rho \le \sqrt{(p-1)/(u-1)}$. Then, with expectations taken under the uniform measure
on $\{0,1\}^n$ and $T_\rho$ the noise operator, the higher $L^u$ norm of the noised
function is bounded by the lower $L^p$ norm of $f$:
\[
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{T_\rho f}^u\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/u} \;\le\;
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^p\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Fix a natural number $n$. Let $1 \le p \le u$ with $u > 1$, and let $\rho$ satisfy $0 \le \rho \le 1$ together
with $\rho \le \sqrt{(p-1)/(u-1)}$. Then for every Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n \to
\bbr$, the noise operator $T_\rho$ contracts the $L^u$ norm below the $L^p$ norm:
\[
\bigl(\E\!\left[\abs{T_\rho f}^u\right]\bigr)^{1/u} \;\le\;
\bigl(\E\!\left[\abs{f}^p\right]\bigr)^{1/p},
\]
where the expectations are taken over the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.general_one_function_hypercontractivity, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_function_iff_two_function_hypercontractivity, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a natural number $n$, real exponents $1 \le p \le u$ with $u \ge 2$, and a noise rate $\rho$ with $0 \le
\rho \le 1$ satisfying $\rho \le \sqrt{(p-1)/(u-1)}$. Then for every pair of Boolean
functions $f, g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$,
\[
  \langle f, T_\rho g\rangle
  \;\le\;
  \bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^{u/(u-1)}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{(u-1)/u}\,
  \bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{g}^{p}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p},
\]
where $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the $L^2$ inner product, $\E$ the expectation, and
$T_\rho$ the noise operator, all taken with respect to the uniform measure on the
hypercube.
\end{theorem}
